author: history_unlimited

item.authorHandle: history_unlimited
item.caption:
JERUSALEM — Israel faces a potentially prolonged political stalemate after parliamentary election exit polls indicated that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot had secured the 61 seats required to control the 120-member Knesset.

Updated projections from Israel’s three principal television networks placed Eisenkot’s opposition bloc at approximately 52 seats and Netanyahu’s coalition at 50, leaving both short of a governing majority. Arab-led parties were projected to secure approximately 18 seats, potentially making their parliamentary support decisive. ￼
Despite Netanyahu’s Likud emerging as the largest individual party, the broader parliamentary arithmetic presents a significant obstacle to forming a stable government.
Official vote counting remains underway. Once results are finalized, President Isaac Herzog is expected to consult parliamentary factions and select the lawmaker most likely to assemble a governing coalition. Negotiations could extend for weeks. If no viable government emerges, Israel could face another election.

HISTORY UNLIMITED OSINT ASSESSMENT: The political uncertainty could carry significant implications for Israel’s future strategy toward Iran, military operations in Gaza, and its security posture along the Lebanese border. However, the exit polls alone do not establish any immediate change in Israeli military policy.
The central question is no longer simply which bloc wins the most seats, but whether either can assemble a functioning parliamentary majority.
Status: Preliminary exit-poll projections, not certified election results.

SOURCES — OCTOBER 27, 2026

1. Associated Press (AP) — Israeli Election Coverage
2. Reuters — Israel Election Results and Coalition Projections
3. The Times of Israel — Channel 12 Exit Poll Coverage
4. The Guardian — Israel Election Live Updates
5. Israel Hayom — Election Exit Poll Results

Note: Exit-poll projections are preliminary and not certified results.

author: saveorchardmesa

item.authorHandle: saveorchardmesa
item.caption:
🗳️ 7 DAYS UNTIL ELECTION DAY — TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 3!
The countdown is on! Make a plan to vote and take time to understand what’s on your ballot.
Swipe through these slides to learn what Ballot Issue 2B would mean for the future of Orchard Mesa Pool.
💧 The proposed increase is just 7 cents on every $100 purchase subject to city sales tax. The measure needs a majority of votes to pass.
📬 Haven’t returned your ballot? Drop it off at an official Mesa County ballot drop box or voter service and polling center. Your ballot must be received by 7 p.m. on Election Day — postmarks don’t count.
📍 Find ballot drop-off locations, voting center hours, and other voter information here:
https://www.mesacounty.us/departments-and-services/clerk-and-recorder/elections/ballot-drop-box-voter-service-and-polling
Take time to review the ballot information for Ballot Issue 2B and vote YES on 2B! ✅
#SaveOrchardMesaPool  #ElectionDay #grandjunctionco #yeson2b

Kellyanne Conway says the battle for the Senate remains anyone's game, with several races polling within the margin of error.

Speaking with @Sean Hannity, Conway explains why President Trump is holding three rallies in just 24 hours, working to energize voters ahead of Election Day.

"I think many of them are going to tip Republican," she predicts.

Election Day is one week away, meaning that it's crunch time for candidates across the country.

On Monday, President Donald Trump campaigned in Mississippi, a state he won by almost 23 points two years ago.

Over the weekend, the battleground state of Michigan saw a political heavyweight bout between Trump and former President Barack Obama.

Liz Landers reports.

item.caption:
Freed from Regime! 🔥
So klang es auf dem Slavija-Platz in Belgrad, als Serbien nach zwölf Jahren Vučić abgewählt hat.

Orbán, Vučić, Kaczyński: Ihre Parteien haben Wahlen oder ihre Mehrheit verloren, an der Wahlurne und bei hoher Wahlbeteiligung. In Brasilien hat Lula sein Amt gegen Bolsonaro verteidigt.

Auch in Israel ist noch alles möglich: Es wird bei Rekordwahlbeteiligung noch ausgezählt, keines der beiden Lager hat bisher eine Mehrheit. Die arabischen Parteien mit rund 16 Sitzen könnten das Zünglein an der Waage sein. Bei Netanjahu ist die Streichung deshalb bewusst zugespitzt, ebenso bei Trump: Er steht am 3. November nicht selbst zur Wahl, bei den Midterms geht es um die Mehrheit im Kongress.

Die Botschaft bleibt: Demokratie ist kein Selbstläufer, aber sie kann gewinnen, wenn Menschen wählen gehen, sich organisieren und nicht resignieren. Kein Land ist verloren, keine Entwicklung unumkehrbar. Und das gilt auch für Deutschland!

Eine andere Zukunft ist möglich! 💚🔥✊

#freedfromdesire #electionday #wahltag

item.caption:
🗳️ I SHOWED UP. I VOTED. MY VOICE MATTERS. 🇺🇸 

Please exercise your right to vote!!!

To those who choose not to vote, I encourage you to think about this: How can we expect change if we don’t participate in the process that helps shape it? You don’t have to agree with everyone, and you don’t have to be passionate about politics every day, but your voice deserves to be heard.

Our communities, our families, our rights, and our future are all affected by decisions made by elected officials. Silence may feel easier, but participation gives us a chance to make our voices count.

I did my part. I showed up and exercised my right to vote. 🇺🇸❤️

Your vote is your voice. Don’t give away the opportunity to use it. 🗳️✨

#ivoted🇺🇸 #ivoted #midtermelections #yourvotematters #yourvoice

Regardless of where we stand politically, we all have a role to play in strengthening our communities.

Key battleground states are also seeing significant early voting activity as the battle for control of Congress enters its final stretch.

🗳 Election Day is around the corner, so it's important to know who is on your ballot. Swipe and scroll to learn about Les McIntosh for Washington County Commissioner! ✅

Pastor Les McIntosh, Sr. is a husband, father, grandfather, small business owner, and community leader running for Washington County Commissioner.

As founder and pastor of Impact Ministries in Hagerstown, he’s spent years working with neighbors facing economic challenges, public safety concerns, and barriers to opportunity. Now, he wants continue to build a strong future for our community with this ‘Back to Basics’ approach.

By tackling the affordability crises, growing the economy with purpose, and bringing needed transparency and accountability to the County Commission, Pastor Les McIntosh, Sr. will put Washington County families first!

Learn more and make your plan to vote at www.mcintoshforus.com

Over the past several weeks, I’ve had the opportunity to knock on doors, meet people, answer questions, and hear what matters most to the families and communities of Ward 2.
I want to sincerely thank everyone who took the time to open their door, have a conversation, share their thoughts, and offer words of encouragement and support. Every conversation has meant a lot to me, and I’m grateful for the opportunity to connect with so many people in our communities!
Today is Election Day! 
If you haven’t voted yet, I encourage you to get out and make your voice heard. Our schools, our students, and the future of Hanover School Division matter, and your vote is an important part of that future.
If you believe in my commitment to our students, families, and communities, I would be honoured to have your support.
📅 Wednesday, October 28 ⏰ Voting is open from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM.
Thank you, Ward 2, for the conversations, the kindness, and the support along the way!
Your vote matters. Your voice matters. Let’s make it count! ✅
#HSDWard2 #HanoverSchoolDivision #ElectionDay #YourVoteMatters

item.caption:
Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Here is a nonpartisan checklist, from official sources:

1. Confirm you're registered. Check your name, address and polling place on your state's election website; USAGov points to vote.gov to start. If you didn't respond to election mail and haven't voted in the last two federal general elections, your registration may be marked inactive.
2. Know your polling place. It's set by your home address and can change from one election to the next. Vote at the wrong place and you may only be able to cast a provisional ballot.
3. Know your ID rules. Each state sets its own, and some let you vote without the ID by signing a form or casting a provisional ballot.

Check yours today at vote.gov, or with your state or local election office. Send this to someone who votes where you do.

We don't endorse candidates or parties. Source: USAGov (usa.gov).

#FloatingFreedom #KnowledgeFindsAWay #ElectionDay #CheckYourRegistration #CivicEngagement

Voters in Tel Aviv have expressed frustration and disappointment after Israeli election results pointed to a political deadlock, with no clear winner emerging.

Israel could face prolonged coalition negotiations or even another election.

"You do not protest by staying home on Election Day. You protest by showing up and voting."

A message to American voters: the ballot box is where frustration should count. Around the world, people fight and even risk their safety for the right to choose their leaders, so the right to vote should never be taken for granted. Staying home may feel like a statement, but it leaves the decision to others — voting is how leaders are held accountable and the future is shaped.

"Your vote is your voice. Your voice is your power. Use it."

author: arielle.lofton

item.authorHandle: arielle.lofton
item.caption:
My son has asked me several times, “Mom, have you voted yet?” ❤️ And Kassidy asked, “Does everyone have to vote?” My response was simple: “No, but those who have the right to vote should.”

As a young Black boy who experienced racism for the first time at just 10 years old, my son understands more than I ever wished he would have to. I’ve taught my children that God created each of us perfectly, that our skin color is never something to be ashamed of, and that every voice matters.

I want them to understand the sacrifices of those who fought for our right to vote. I’m simply trying to lead by example, raising children who know their worth, stand firm in their faith, and understand the power of their voices.

Voting is a right and a privilege I don’t take lightly. Get out and vote! Your voice matters! 🇺🇸❤️ #IVoted ❤️

Voting by mail? Do NOT let your ballot go to waste. Swipe ⬅️ for 5️⃣ things you need to know!

1️⃣ Find your ballot. Still haven’t received it? Contact your election office for a replacement, or plan to vote in person.
2️⃣ Fill it out ASAP. Read every instruction. Some states require a witness or notary.
3️⃣ Skip the mailbox if you can. Hand-deliver it to a drop box, your election office or a polling place.
4️⃣ Have to mail it? Go today. Take it to the post office counter and ask for it to be postmarked right then.
5️⃣ Track your ballot until it’s counted.

Make your plan at BPACDemocracyToolkit.com🔗

#BPAC #VoteByMail #Vote2026 #ElectionDay

author: keyhrpeo

item.authorHandle: keyhrpeo
item.caption:
Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Nonpartisan reminder for Florida employers: now is the time to decide how your schedule will handle it.

Florida doesn't have a general law requiring private employers to give time off to vote. But a lot of employees will still ask, especially those with long shifts or commutes. Early voting and mail ballots help, but only if people know their shift in advance.

The simple move: post the schedule early, tell your team how to request a change, and apply the same answer to everyone. Consistency is what keeps a scheduling question from turning into an HR problem.

👉 keyhrs.com
#ElectionDay #FloridaBusiness #HRTips #WorkplacePolicy #SmallBusiness

author: repcruzwi

item.authorHandle: repcruzwi
item.caption:
🗳️ KNOW YOUR RIGHTS: TIME OFF TO VOTE

Election Day is almost here, and Wisconsin workers have a right many employers overlook. Under Wis. Stat. 6.76(1), you can be absent from work for up to 3 hours to vote. No exceptions.

Here’s what you need to know:

✅ Your employer must allow you up to 3 hours away from work to vote.
✅ The Wisconsin Elections Commission has confirmed that simply making sure you have 3 hours between the end of your shift and poll closing at 8:00 p.m. is NOT enough.
✅ Employers aren’t required to pay you for that time, but they cannot penalize you in any other way for using it.

⚠️ Violations are punishable by a fine of up to $1,000, up to six months in jail, or both.

My office recently heard from a constituent about an employer’s questionable time-off-to-vote policy. That’s deeply concerning, especially for people who work long hours, have long commutes, or can’t get to the polls after work.

What you can do now:
✅Learn your employer’s policy before Election Day.
✅ If a policy interferes with your right to vote, consider filing a complaint with the Wisconsin Elections Commission.
✅ Contact my office. I stand ready to help. Call (608) 237-9162 or email rep.cruz@legis.wisconsin.gov

Voting is a fundamental right, and infringement on that right is unacceptable.

#KnowYourRights #WorkersRights #VoteWI #ElectionDay #WIleg

Attached: Press Release from the Office of Rep Cruz and Wisconsin Elections Commission formal advisory opinion

I voted early, and I voted Democratic! 🗳️💙

I’m remembering the history behind this right. The 19th Amendment expanded women’s voting rights in 1920, but many Black women still faced discriminatory barriers. Generations of activists fought to break those barriers, helping secure the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

People marched, sacrificed, and risked their lives so our voices could be heard. Today, I honored that legacy by casting my ballot and making my own choice. My voice matters. My vote counts. ✊🏾🇺🇸

#IVoted #EarlyVoting #VotedDemocratic

Also setting up an actual recording space for some video content coming soon!

Anywho, that’s all for now. Stay chill out there! ✌️

author: federalistpapersproject

item.authorHandle: federalistpapersproject
item.caption:
You don't get to be shocked by an election you skipped. 🗳️

Midterms are Tuesday, November 3.

Since WWII, the president's party has lost House seats in 18 of 20 midterms. Why? The winning side gets comfortable and stays home.

Right now, Democrats are outpacing Republicans in early voting in states that track party registration.

Republicans hold the House by a handful of seats. Lose it, and it's two years of investigations, impeachment, and a stalled agenda.

There's no do-over until 2028.

Check your registration. Find your polling place. Bring a friend. Vote red. 🇺🇸

👇 Be honest, who in your life needs a nudge to vote this year?

#Midterms2026 #ElectionDay #VoteRed #Vote #GOP #Republicans #Conservative #ElectionsHaveConsequences #TheFederalistPapers

item.caption:
🗳️ Still have your ballot in El Paso County? Don’t mail it. Drop it in an official ballot box or vote in person.

⏰ Your ballot must reach the clerk by 7 p.m. Tuesday, Nov. 3. Postmarks don’t count. If you’re in line by 7 p.m., you can still vote.

📱 Track your ballot with BallotTrax. If you received a signature letter, text COLORADO to 28683 to fix it from your phone.

Find locations and hours on the El Paso County Clerk’s election page and share this with someone who still has their ballot.

author: alvarezh3

item.authorHandle: alvarezh3
item.caption:
Yesterday, on the final day of early voting, I made my voice heard. 🗳️

Our comeback is sponsored by God. Our faith is strong, and our voice matters.

As a professor, I teach that democracy is more than a lesson in a textbook—it’s a responsibility. As a father and community member, I know the future depends on the choices we make today.

James Baldwin wrote, “The place in which I’ll fit will not exist until I make it.”

To my students, family, and community: Don’t let anything stand between you and your right to be heard. Not fear. Not obstacles. Not discouragement.

🗳️ Election Day is November 3. Make a plan. Show up. Make your voice count.

I voted. Now, I’m encouraging you to do the same.

#IVoted #November3 #MakeYourVoiceHeard #DemocracyInAction

It’s never been a secret where my political feelings lie and it never will be! vote like your rights depends on it!! there are so many other pieces to the puzzle but voting is an important and easily actionable step!

Early voting ends October, 31st in NC and election day is November, 3rd!  Remember you can still register during early voting but not on election day in NC 💙

We don’t have these on the site, but we do still have our f*** 🧊 collection! so check those out if you’re feeling a little angry like we are this week!

item.caption:
🇺🇸 I VOTED TODAY! 🇺🇸💪
I voted for a STRONG America 🇺🇸, a STRONG Closter 🏡, and a STRONG Board of Education 📚!
I voted to honor every man and woman who has served in our military, courageously fought for our country, and sacrificed so much to protect our freedom. ❤️🤍💙
I voted because their sacrifices must never be forgotten, and the freedoms they fought for must never be taken for granted. We owe it to our veterans, our fallen heroes, and future generations to protect the values that make America great.
I voted for leadership, accountability, strong communities, and a brighter future for our children. I believe we must stand up for our country, protect our values, and make sure America remains strong, safe, and free. 💪🇺🇸
NOW IT'S YOUR TURN! 🗳️
📣 MAKE YOUR VOICE HEARD! Get out and vote for the future you believe in—for America, for Closter, and for our children!
🇺🇸 God Bless America! ❤️🤍💙
#IVoted #AmericaFirst #StrongAmerica #StrongCloster #SupportOurVeterans ElectionDay ClosterNJ StrongBOE GodBlessAmerica

item.authorHandle: pmlanning
item.caption:
🗳️ I VOTED! 🇺🇸

Doing my little part to help a few folks in Washington update their résumés. 😂👋

Because apparently, you can’t just hit the “unsubscribe” button on bad leadership. 🤷‍♀️

All jokes aside, I voted for kindness, compassion, decency, and a future where we spend more time lifting people up than tearing each other down.

We don’t have to agree on everything to treat each other with respect. ❤️

But seriously… some of these politicians have overstayed their welcome. Time for some fresh faces and fresh ideas! 😂

Love your neighbor. Stand up for what you believe in. And never underestimate the power of your vote. 🇺🇸💙

#IVoted #DemocracyMatters #VoteForChange #KindnessMatters

author: iu_asianculturecenter

item.authorHandle: iu_asianculturecenter
item.caption:
🗳️ ROAD TO ELECTION DAY: FLOOD THE POLLS 2026 !!!! 

The ACC is teaming up with IU Student Government, the Neal-Marshall Black Culture Center, La Casa, the LGBTQ+ Culture Center, and IU NAACP for a week of community, conversation, and civic engagement. Here’s what’s coming up:

🍬 Oct 29 | No Tricks, Just Treats and Relaxation
4:30 PM, NMBCC Library
Relax, unwind, or catch up on work before Homecoming. Voting resources will be available too!

✊🏽 Nov 2 | March for Us Solidarity Walk
6:30 PM, Neal-Marshall Courtyard to Sample Gates
Sponsored by IU NAACP. Join us in showing solidarity with the family of Nolan Wells and others seeking justice in the wake of racial violence.

🗳️ Nov 3 | Flood the Polls: Election Day!
10 AM-4 PM, participating culture centers (including the ACC!)
Stop by one or more of the culture centers for snacks, resources, and conversations about the importance of civic participation.

Come connect, engage, and share your voice 💙

#FloodThePolls #IUVotes #IUACC #AsianCultureCenter #IUBloomington #IndianaUniversity #ElectionDay

author: spectrum_cs

item.authorHandle: spectrum_cs
item.caption:
🗳️ Your voice matters at every age!

Election Day is coming up on Tuesday, November 3, and the Alameda County Advisory Commission on Aging is helping older adults feel informed and prepared to cast their ballots.

The decisions we make at the ballot box can have a real impact on the programs and services older adults rely on—from transportation and caregiving resources to healthcare, nutrition, and Meals on Wheels.

Not sure where to start? Swipe through for helpful information on:
✓ Getting ready to vote
✓ Understanding what may appear on your ballot
✓ Common election terms
✓ Finding trusted, nonpartisan voter information

Need assistance? Visit vote411.org or contact the Alameda County Registrar of Voters at (510) 272-6933 for trusted guidance.

Take a few minutes to get informed, make a plan, and make your voice heard this Election Day! 🇺🇸

#SpectrumCommunityServices #AlamedaCounty #OlderAdults #ElectionDay  #StrongerTogether

item.authorHandle: gaiafamilyofficial
item.caption:
IVF is on the ballot in Virginia.

On November 3, 2026, Virginians vote on Question 1, a constitutional amendment that would add a fundamental right to reproductive freedom, including decisions about fertility care like IVF.

Right now, reproductive healthcare in Virginia is protected by statute, which means future legislative majorities can change it. A yes vote would place these protections in Virginia’s Bill of Rights and protect doctors, nurses, and patients.

For anyone going through IVF now or planning to in the future, the right to fertility care wouldn't depend on who controls Richmond.

How to vote in Virginia:

Early, in-person voting continues through Saturday, October 31
Election Day is Tuesday, November 3

Check your registration and polling place at elections.virginia.gov or vote.gov

Share this with a Virginian who should know.

#Reproductiverights #IVF #VirginiaVotes #ElectionDay #Gaiafamily

item.authorHandle: pbsnews
item.caption:
With one week until Election Day, the final push is on.

President Donald Trump on Tuesday made a swing through Texas, a state Republicans have long counted on, but where Democrats see an opportunity to make gains.

With voters pointing to the cost of everyday necessities, the economy is looming large in the final week of the campaign.

Lisa Desjardins reports.

#Democrats #Republicans #midtermelection #Trump #news #politics

author: kappaphi_aka

item.authorHandle: kappaphi_aka
item.caption:
ELECTION DAY IS LESS THAN A WEEK AWAY! 🗳️

If you’re 18 or older, your vote is your opportunity to have a say in the changes you want to see.

BUT LET’S TALK…

- Are you confused about elections?
- Unsure about your local candidates or what they stand for?
- Ever thought, “Why vote? My vote won’t make a difference anyway.”

The ladies of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated®, Kappa Phi Chapter invite ALL students to an open and engaging conversation with Legislator Vivian L. Russell and Kadeem Brown so you can gain the tools to make informed decision in your own community. 

We’re asking the questions YOU want answered from understanding political campaigns and making informed decisions to what really happens when people don’t vote. 

Bring your questions. Bring your opinions. Bring your friends. Already voted…come anyway and join the conversation 

📅 November 2 at 8 PM
📍 Student Center Greenhouse
👗 Business Attire Encouraged! (Not Mandatory)

#KappaPhi #AKA1908 #ElectionDay #YourPowerYourVote

🇺🇸 I VOTED! 🗳️❤️🤍💙

Because my voice matters. My vote matters. And the future of our communities matters!

Voting is more than exercising a right; it’s an opportunity to have a voice in the decisions that impact our families, our communities, and generations to come.

As a woman, a mother, a business owner, and a community leader, I understand the importance of showing up, not just when change is needed, but when we have the opportunity to help shape it.

We cannot advocate for change while remaining silent when it’s time to make our voices heard!

Today, I exercised my right, honored those who fought for that right, and did my part to help shape the future.

✨ Your voice is powerful. Your vote is your voice. USE IT!

item.caption:
🇺🇸 I MADE MY CHOICE. DID YOU? 🗳️

MY VOICE. MY CHOICE. MY FUTURE. ❤️🤍💙

I was born in Ukraine, and today I'm proud to call America my home. 🇺🇦❤️🇺🇸
I still remember the first time I voted. It wasn't just about checking a box or choosing a candidate. It was about realizing that my voice mattered. That I had the freedom to make my own decisions and take responsibility for my future.
And that feeling has never left me.
Life has taught me one important lesson: FREEDOM SHOULD NEVER BE TAKEN FOR GRANTED.

Democracy doesn't depend on how close you are to the ballot box. It depends on whether you choose to make your voice heard.

Whether you're across the street, across the state, or across the world — your voice still matters! 🌎

Never let anyone think for you, speak for you, or decide your future on your behalf.

We all have different opinions, different beliefs, and different dreams. And that's the beauty of freedom — the right to make our own choices.
This time, I voted by mail because distance should never silence my voice. 📬🇺🇸
Don't let others decide your future while you remain silent.

YOUR VOICE IS YOUR POWER.
YOUR CHOICE IS YOUR FREEDOM.
YOUR VOTE IS YOUR RIGHT.

Freedom is more than a privilege. It's a responsibility.
You don't have to follow the crowd. You don't have to agree with everyone. But you should always have the courage to stand for what you believe in.

🇺🇸 I MADE MY CHOICE. DID YOU?

author: joelmarroquinc13

item.authorHandle: joelmarroquinc13
item.caption:
🇺🇸🗳️ I Voted! ¡Ya voté ❤️ ❤️ ❤️ 

Hoy voté por mis valores y por un cambio en California. Voté por Steve Hilton por la familia, por los niños que aún no han nacido y por una educación donde nuestros hijos vayan a aprender, sin imposiciones ideológicas.

Respeto a la comunidad LGBT porque yo también vengo de ella. Tengo muchos amigos gays a quienes amo y quiero, aunque no siempre pensemos igual. Cada quien tiene sus luchas, así como yo tengo la mía con mi identidad cada día. Creo que los padres deben tener voz en la educación de sus hijos y que los niños puedan tomar sus propias decisiones sobre su identidad y cambios de sexo cuando cumplan 18 años, sin presiones.

Antes me identificaba más con la izquierda, hoy me considero conservador, aunque no comparto todas las posturas de la derecha.

Ser conservador no significa estar en contra de los inmigrantes. Sigo apoyando una reforma migratoria justa para quienes han trabajado y se han esforzado por salir adelante en este país.

Los que me conocen en persona saben quién soy, conocen mis valores, mis convicciones y cómo soy realmente como persona. Saben cuánto amo y respeto a nuestra comunidad migrante y que nunca olvido mis raíces.

No voté por presión ni por quedar bien con nadie. Pensar diferente no me hace racista ni homofóbico. Si no me conoces, no puedes juzgarme solamente por mi voto.

Podemos pensar diferente y seguir respetándonos. De eso también se trata vivir en democracia. 🇺🇸❤️

#YaVote #IVoted #California2026 #VoteRed #MyVoteMyVoice

item.authorHandle: moore_shantay
item.caption:
🗳️✅ I DID MY PART! DID YOU?! ❤️🙌🏽

Y'all, I just finished EARLY VOTING, and let me tell you something... I'M PROUD OF MYSELF! 🥰👏🏽

I'm still young, okay?! 😂 I might be in my 30s, but BABYYYY, I'm still young enough to understand that MY VOICE MATTERS! 💃🏽🤣

And let me tell y'all, the line was SHORT! I was in and out in about FIVE MINUTES! ⏰👏🏽

Sometimes we get so caught up in our everyday lives that we forget how important it is to make our voices heard.

You don't have to agree with everybody. You don't have to vote the way somebody else votes. But you DO have the right to make your OWN decisions! ❤️

YOUR VOICE MATTERS. YOUR OPINION MATTERS. YOUR VOTE MATTERS! 🗳️💯

So if you're registered and eligible, take advantage of EARLY VOTING while you can! Check your local voting hours and locations, and make a plan that works for you.

Because one thing about me... I'm not just going to sit back and talk about what I want to see happen. I'm going to participate, too! 🙌🏽

Now let me ask y'all something... WHO ALREADY VOTED, AND WHO'S PLANNING TO VOTE?! 👀🗳️

#IVoted #EarlyVoting #YourVoiceMatters #EveryVoteCounts #CivicEngagement #ProudVoter

item.caption:
🗳️ ALABAMA, YOUR VOTE MATTERS! 🇺🇸

Friendly reminder: Election Day is next Tuesday, November 3, 2026! You still have time to educate yourself on the candidates and the 4 proposed Constitutional Amendments before heading to the polls.

Your vote can impact everything from water bills and public safety to local schools and the future of your community. 🏫 Your voice matters, and voting is one way to make sure it’s heard!

DON’T WAIT UNTIL ELECTION DAY TO GET INFORMED. Make a plan, review your ballot, and know who and what you’re voting for.

🗳️ Visit AlabamaVotes.gov or check the link in our bio to learn more about the candidates, their roles, term lengths, and to access your county’s sample ballot.

Your community. Your future. Your vote. ❤️🤍💙

#AlabamaVotes #ElectionDay #YourVoteMatters #GetOutAndVote

item.caption:
6 days left. Before you scroll past, check 3 things tonight. 🗳️

1. Mail ballot still on your counter? Don’t mail it this late. Hand it in at a drop box or your election office.
2. Not sure you’re registered? It takes 2 minutes. 21 states and DC let you register and vote the same day.
3. Early voting ends this week in a lot of states. Swipe for your last day, or find your polling place for Tuesday, Nov 3.

All three links are at CanIVote.org. When you vote, bring your guide from bluevoterguide.org. Then send this to the friend who always says they’ll vote “later.”
#VoteEarly #Midterms2026 #EfficientActivist #GetOutTheVote #ElectionDay

item.caption:
🗳️ Today is Election Day in Manitoba!⁠
⁠
Your municipal vote helps shape the services and decisions that affect your everyday life, from road maintenance and garbage collection to local schools and community services.⁠
⁠
✅ Before you head to the polls:⁠
📍 Check your voting location with your municipality⁠
🪪 Bring valid ID showing your name and current address⁠
📋 Learn about the candidates and issues on your ballot⁠
⏰ Polls are open from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM⁠
⁠
Not on the voters list? If you’re eligible, you can still register in person and vote on Election Day. Be sure to bring valid identification!⁠
⁠
Make your plan to vote and make your voice heard. Every level of government matters, and civic engagement starts in our own communities.⁠
⁠
#ManitobaElection #ElectionDay #CivicEngagement #MunicipalElections #YourVoiceYourVote #TheCanadianMuslimVote

author: mteilearn

item.authorHandle: mteilearn
item.caption:
Democracy is built long before Election Day. And according to MTEI Graduate Professor Michal Muszkat-Barkan (Cohort 4), much of that work begins in the classroom.

In a timely article for the  @JewishJournal, Michal explores how educators can help prepare the next generation for democratic participation by teaching them how to engage with disagreement, examine competing claims, and listen to different perspectives.

As Michal writes, “Elections can replace governments. They cannot, by themselves, teach citizens how to live with disagreement.”

With elections on people's minds in both Israel and the United States, her piece echoes MTEI's principle of “How We Talk Matters,” reminding us of the important role educators play in helping students navigate difficult conversations, engage thoughtfully with differing perspectives, and learn to disagree respectfully.

Read Michal's full article, “Democracy Is Built Before Election Day” >> 
link in bio

Early voting numbers in Tarrant County are showing an interesting trend ahead of the Nov. 3 election.
Voters with a history of participating in Democratic primaries are turning out at higher rates than those with a Republican primary voting history. But leaders from both parties have different predictions about what those numbers mean for Election Day.

author: goodmorningucla

item.authorHandle: goodmorningucla
item.caption:
You heard Bill, VOTE! Election Day is November 3rd and here’s everything you need to know about where and when to vote on or near campus!
Voting centers will be open at De Neve Plaza (Rooms P352 & P353), Hammer Museum (Annenberg Terrace), and Ackerman Union (Bruin Reception Room) from October 31 through November 3. Hours are 10 AM to 7 PM from October 31 to November 2 and 7 AM to 8 PM on Election Day. The Ackerman Union Grand Ballroom will also be open on November 2 from 10 AM to 7 PM.

Although the last day to register to vote online was Oct. 19th, it’s still not too late to register through the “Same Day” voter registration office. There will even be donuts given out on Bruin Walk for students who register to vote on Nov. 2nd!

Ballot drop boxes are available 24 hours a day at the UCLA Parking and Information Kiosk and Westwood Branch Library. Both close at 8 PM on Election Day.

For additional voting locations and election information, follow @BruinsVote or visit LAVote.gov. Go Vote, Bruins!

#UCLA #UCLABruins #ElectionDay #Vote #ImJustABill

item.authorHandle: thestella_maxwell
item.caption:
🇺🇸 WE VOTED! 🇺🇸

For me, voting is so much more than checking a box on a ballot. It is a privilege I will never take for granted.

Having been born and raised under communism in Romania and having experienced life under socialism, I know firsthand that freedom is not something to take lightly. I understand what it means to live in a system that limits freedom and personal choice.

That is why living in America is such a privilege and an honor to me!

I am deeply grateful to live in a country where my voice matters, where I have the freedom to express my beliefs, practice my faith, and participate in choosing the leaders who will shape our nation’s future.

My vote reflects my convictions, my values, my faith, and my gratitude for the freedoms we have as Americans. I vote with a heart that remembers where I came from and a deep appreciation for the opportunities and liberties I have today.

Freedom is precious. Democracy is a responsibility. And the right to vote is a privilege that should never be taken for granted.

May God bless America, protect our freedoms, grant wisdom to our leaders, and guide our nation back to Him. 

I am thankful to call America home! 

#IVoted #GodBlessAmerica #FreedomIsAPrivilege #GratefulToBeAmerican #FaithFreedomAndCountry

Early voting continues **October 28–30**, with **Friday, October 30** being the final day to cast your ballot early.

 Make a plan, know where to vote, and make your voice heard.

Election Day is almost here. On Tuesday, Nov. 3, voters across the country will head to the polls to decide federal, state and local races.

All eyes will be on states where redistricting has reshaped congressional maps, as #voters will determine whether district lines drawn to benefit Republicans or Democrats fulfill each party's hopes to flip more seats in their favor.

#Voting is a fundamental part of civic participation, but it often takes a little preparation. From registration deadlines to voting rules and polling locations, here's what you need to know before #ElectionDay.

Read more at the link in our bio.

📸: Veronica Bravo, USA TODAY

IMPORTANT ELECTION DAY REMINDER! 🗳️

🚫 Polling place sites will NOT have mail-in ballot drop boxes on Election Day.

📍 Where can you drop off your mail-in ballot?

• Maywood Courthouse: 1311 Maybrook Square, Maywood
• Bridgeview Courthouse: 10220 S. 76th Ave., Bridgeview
• Cook County Clerk’s Office – Downtown: 69 W. Washington Street, Chicago
• Other locations: Markham, Skokie and Rolling Meadows courthouses

✅ Don't wait until the last minute! Plan ahead to ensure your ballot gets where it needs to go.

📢 Please share this reminder with friends, family and neighbors!

#ElectionDay  #MakeAPlan

item.caption:
Out on the doors in Brunswick yesterday with Devin Lander and @Chloe Pierce! 🗳️🍁

There is nothing better than hitting the pavement, meeting neighbors right at their front doors, and hearing directly about what matters most to you and your families. From local issues to the big picture, these conversations are what community representation is all about.

Thank you to everyone who took the time to chat with us yesterday and every day! If we missed you on your street, make sure you have a plan to get out and vote. Early voting lasts through Sunday and Election Day is Tuesday!

author: offtheclocknurse

item.authorHandle: offtheclocknurse
item.caption:
Don’t forget to vote. 
.
.
For the air you breathe... The water you drink... The people you love... The healthcare you need... The rights we deserve... The children who will inherit this world... The strangers whose lives may look nothing like yours.
.
.
Your vote affects more than just you.
.
.
You don’t have to be a political expert to be an informed voter, but you do have to be willing to do a little homework. Read the propositions. Understand what a YES or NO vote actually means. Look beyond the headlines... Question what you hear, verify what you read, and take the time to understand the potential consequences of the decisions you're making.
.
.
A ballot measure can sound great in its title but have implications you never considered. That’s why it matters to understand the details, not just the talking points.
.
.
And please, remember that the ability to vote is an opportunity to have a say in not just  the country we live in, but the world we live in... Don't take that lightly.
.
.
We won't all agree on every issue. But we should all care enough to be informed, to think critically, and to recognize that our decisions can affect people beyond ourselves.
.
.
VOTE for the things you believe in, the people you care about, the future you want to see....But above all, know what you're voting for.
.
.
Your vote is your voice. Use it thoughtfully. 🇺🇸

item.caption:
This was cool:

I voted early in Houston County GA on Oct 14th. There was no line, and maybe 10 voters in the booths.

Every time a first-time voter checked in, the volunteer poll workers announced it.

FIVE brand new voters showed up.

Everyone broke into applause!🎉🍑🇺🇲

item.caption:
Missed the mail? Drop it off. 🗳️

6 days to Election Day, and more than 35 million early and mail votes are already in, on pace with the 2018 record.

The safe mail-by date has passed, so if your ballot is still on the counter, take it to an official drop box or your county elections office, or vote in person. Young voters are showing up too: youth registration is up from 2022, and most new young voters are unaffiliated.

Check your status and find your drop box at vote.gov, then wear the sticker proudly.

author: luminous360booth

item.authorHandle: luminous360booth
item.caption:
ONE VOTE. ONE VOICE. ONE PROUD GRANDMA! 

Today wasn’t just about casting my vote… it was about showing my grandson what it looks like to SHOW UP and let your voice be heard!

ONE LITTLE HICCUP TURNED INTO AN UNEXPECTED TRIP TO THE DMV! 

Y’all!!! How in the world did I let my driver’s license expire 32 DAYS AGO?! 

Here I am thinking I’m handling business, checking things off my to-do list, and living my best life… only to discover my license had been expired for over a MONTH! 

Well, there was nothing left to do but head straight to the DMV and get that situation handled! 

DMV visit complete!
License renewed!
Temporary driving certificate in hand!
One less thing to worry about!

Sometimes life has a funny way of reminding you that even when you’re busy taking care of EVERYTHING and EVERYBODY ELSE… you better check on your OWN business too! 

Consider this your friendly reminder to CHECK THAT EXPIRATION DATE! 

Now, somebody please tell me I’m not the only one who’s ever let their license expire without realizing it!

author: cpochyla

item.authorHandle: cpochyla
item.caption:
🗳️ VOTE EARLY. Because Future You Cannot Be Trusted. 🗳️

Sure, you plan to vote on Election Day. But let's be honest about what could go wrong between now and then:

🦝 A raccoon moves into your garage and you're now legally obligated to negotiate with him.
🧦 You lose one sock and spend the entire day searching, because you refuse to live like that.
📺 You start "one episode" of a new show. You emerge four days later with a beard and no sense of time.
🍕 The pizza place gets your order wrong and you have to have a conversation about it.
🐈 Your cat sits on you. You cannot move. Those are the rules.
🚗 Your car makes a new noise and you need a full day to stare at it with your hood up like you know things.
🎂 You get invited to a coworker's birthday cake in the break room and lose all ability to leave.
😴 You take a "quick 20-minute nap" and wake up in a different decade.
👵 Your aunt calls "real quick." See you next Thursday.

Life is unpredictable. Your ballot doesn't have to be. 🙌

The polls are open now and will be open Thursday and Friday from 7:00a.m-7:00pm. I’m at Frisco Fire Station 6 today so come say “hi”

Vote early. Then go find that sock. 🧦✅

#VoteEarly #ElectionDay #DoItNowDealWithTheRaccoonLater

item.authorHandle: dannypintauro
item.caption:
Well, I voted! 🗳️🇺🇸

And because apparently I can’t go anywhere without ending up in front of a camera, I got stopped by a news crew on my way out and interviewed about Proposition 40! 😂 

No idea who they were, so if you happen to see me on some random news channel, let me know!

I actually spent a good amount of time researching everything on the ballot, so I had PLENTY to say. LOL.

But one thing I told the reporter that I really believe is that even if you think your vote won’t make a difference, VOTE ANYWAY! Sometimes it’s not just about whether something passes or fails. author: catandrajones

item.authorHandle: catandrajones
item.caption:
🗳️ MY VOTE. MY VOICE. MY POWER.

I’ve heard all the debates about voting versus sitting this election out. And I understand the frustration. No politician has a perfect record of delivering for the Black community.

But here’s where I stand: Sitting out doesn’t make the decisions go away. It just means they’re made without your voice.

Let me make one thing clear: VOTING MATTERS. YOUR VOTE COUNTS. AND YOUR VOICE IS HEARD! Especially during MIDTERM ELECTIONS, when decisions are made about who represents us in Congress, state government, and our local communities.

Don’t underestimate the power of your ONE vote. Elections can be decided by incredibly small margins, and every ballot contributes to the outcome.

Voting isn’t about blind loyalty to a politician or a political party. It’s about accountability, representation, and having a say in the policies that affect our everyday lives.

I exercised my right to vote, and I encourage everyone eligible to make their voice heard, too.

📍 MARYLAND VOTERS: Early voting is underway, and Election Day is November 3!

📌 QUESTION 3: This proposed constitutional amendment concerns congressional redistricting. Voting FOR supports the amendment; voting AGAINST rejects it. Read it, understand it, and make an informed choice.

Your vote matters. Your voice counts. And your participation is POWER. ✊🏾🗳️

#IVoted #MarylandVotes #MidtermElections #YourVoteMatters #BlackCivicEngagement EarlyVoting Election2026 Question3

author: iamerickbowens

item.authorHandle: iamerickbowens
item.caption:
🗳️ MY VOTE IS IN! 🇺🇸

One thing about me, I believe in living what you preach! I never want to encourage others to do something that I’m not willing to do myself.

And let me tell y’all, today tested that commitment! 😂 Between the runaround, unexpected inconveniences, and having to exercise a little extra patience, getting my vote in was a JOURNEY! But I was determined not to let the obstacles become my excuse.

I made it happen, and my vote is IN! 🙌🏽

I believe our responsibility goes beyond talking about what we want to see happen. We have to be willing to participate in the process.

So whatever you do, GET OUT AND VOTE! 🗳️

Do your research. Make informed decisions. Exercise your right to vote.

Your voice matters. Your vote matters. And your participation matters! 

#IVoted #YourVoteMatters #ExerciseYourRight #MoreGrace #Forward

author: imtiyazrazak

item.authorHandle: imtiyazrazak
item.caption:
Votes are being counted in Israel. According to exit polls, Netanyahu’s Likud party is projected to win more seats than any other party. The Arab-Muslim coalition is projected to secure between 18 and 20 seats—a historic milestone.

Democracy functions best when it includes minorities. As a political scientist, I welcome the participation of Arab Israelis in the electoral process. Israel’s political system allows them to exercise their voting rights—a freedom often restricted in many Muslim-majority countries, where non-Muslims are sometimes treated as second-class citizens.

Countries across the Middle East need to embrace democracy. Authoritarian governments may deliver economic gains, as China demonstrates, but those gains do not justify political repression. Regimes such as those in Iran and North Korea have limited economic opportunities while suppressing dissent.

Democracy is not perfect, but it remains the best system of government we have.

Khadija Khan #Israel #democracy #vote #ElectionDay

item.caption:
🗳️🇺🇸 COME VOTE WITH ME!

Come along with me to see how long it actually takes us to vote! 👀🗳️

Just a friendly reminder that early voting ends this Saturday, October 31st, and Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd!

Your voice matters, your vote matters, and every vote counts! ❤️

Take a little time out of your day, do your research, and get out there and make a difference! 🙌🏼🇺🇸

¡Hagamos escuchar nuestra voz! 🗳️❤️

#GoVote #EarlyVoting #OklahomaVotes #YourVoteMatters #TulsaOklahoma

One of the freedoms we have as Americans is the opportunity to make our voices heard through our vote. 🇺🇸

We may not all share the same opinions or beliefs, and that’s okay. What matters is that we have the freedom to participate in the process.

I exercised my right to vote today!

Early voting in Nevada ends this Friday, October 30.

No political debates here. Just a friendly reminder to exercise your right, make your voice heard, and never take that freedom for granted.

#IVoted #EarlyVoting #NevadaVotes #YourVoiceMatters #ThisChristianVotes

author: drrobynshort

item.authorHandle: drrobynshort
item.caption:
How the matriarchy votes. 🌅

Not against an enemy. For a vision.

For a world where power is shared, not hoarded. Where the most vulnerable among us (children, elders, the sick, the poor, the newly arrived, and the earth itself) are protected. Where leaders guide through care, not fear.

Before you vote on Tuesday, hold every name on your ballot up to these six questions. And I mean every name. School boards, city councils, judges, and county commissioners shape our daily lives as much as the names at the top.

I’m not telling you which party to vote for. I’m asking you to vote for the world our grandmothers dreamed of and our grandchildren deserve.

Save this. Share it to your stories. Send it to three people heading to the polls. Offer a ride, or watch someone’s kids so they can vote.

Then keep building on November 4.

My new essay, “The Rise of the Matriarchy,” is on The Matriarchal Way. Link in bio. DrRobynShort.Substack.com

#TheMatriarchalWay #TheMatriarchEffect #Matriarchy #PowerWith #VoteYourValues #ElectionDay #Vote2026 #WomenLeaders #MatriarchalLeadership #DignityForAll #BuildTheMatriarchy

author: countyoftulare

item.authorHandle: countyoftulare
item.caption:
6 days until Election Day!

Did you know? The barcode on your vote by mail ballot return envelope connects to your voter record, helps prevent double voting, and keeps your choices private.

Before a ballot is accepted for counting, elections staff scans the return envelope and records its receipt. Next, they compare the envelope signature with signatures on your voter record. Last, they check whether you have already voted to prevent more than one ballot from being counted for the same voter.

Return your vote by mail ballot now or vote in person at your polling place on November 3! Find all polling places at https://ow.ly/c9Eg5101VlV.

#TulareCounty #ElectionDay #Vote @tularevote

author: tara.a.haugen

item.authorHandle: tara.a.haugen
item.caption:
🇺🇸I’M JUST GOING TO SAY IT…🇺🇸

If you’ve got time to complain about politics, argue on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, etc., and tell everyone what’s wrong with this country…then you’ve got time to GO VOTE!🗳️

Because here’s the deal…👇🏻

I don’t care if you’re Republican, Democrat, Independent, or somewhere in between.❤️🤍💙

I don’t care WHO you vote for. I care THAT you vote!👌🏻

You don’t have to agree with me. I don’t have to agree with you. That’s the beauty of living in a country where we have the freedom to make our own choices!🫶🏻

But if you can’t be bothered to exercise your right to vote, don’t be surprised when someone asks where all that political passion was on Election Day.🤷🏼‍♀️

Your voice matters. Your vote matters. And your right to vote is something worth exercising!🇺🇸

So do your research, know what’s on your ballot, and make your voice heard!📢

And remember…

DON’T JUST BITCH ABOUT IT. VOTE ABOUT IT!☑️

#GoVote #YourVoiceMatters #ElectionDay #ExerciseYourRight #Vote2026

OBAMA IN THE A! 

President Barack Obama is back in Atlanta, and the energy is REAL!

Somebody said OBAMA 2028! 😂

Now, Georgia, let’s talk about November 3!

Early voting ends Friday, October 30, but Election Day is Tuesday, November 3!

If you’ve already voted, don’t stop there. Call your family. Text your friends. Check on your neighbors. Make sure the people you love have a plan to vote.

The energy doesn’t end at a rally. Civic participation means showing up when it counts.

Georgia, Election Day is November 3. Polls are open from 7 AM to 7 PM.

#ObamaInAtlanta #GeorgiaVotes #ElectionDay2026 #BarackObama #PolishedInPolitics

item.authorHandle: iecsouthafrica
item.caption:
🗳️VOTING STATIONS ARE FOR VOTING, NOT CAMPAIGNING

On Election Day, political candidates, party leaders, and party agents are strictly prohibited from wearing political party regalia inside voting stations. 

Why? 
Because a voting station must provide a neutral environment where every voter can make their choice freely, without being influenced, pressured, or intimidated. 

What about voters? 
As a voter, you have the right to wear your party regalia to vote. However, no active campaigning, rallying, or distribution of party materials is allowed by anyone within the voting station boundaries.

When you arrive, the focus should remain entirely on your right to cast your ballot freely and in secret. 

#LGE2026 #GetUpShowUpVote #ElectionDay #YourVoteYourChoice

item.authorHandle: thomas_shute_
item.caption:
Had a blast last night at the Obama, Ossoff, KLB really in Morrow, Georgia! It was really something special and a one in a lifetime experience to hear them speak, and to be in the same room as president Obama! After 3 hours of waiting in line to get in, Barack Obama's motorcade drive by and he waived his hand at the crowd, which triggered a full on stampede to get into security and make the cut off, leaving us packed like sardenes figuring out how to handle this and who to get through the line. Eventually I was able to get in and it was total energy! Honestly, I couldn't have asked for a better time and night wish seemed as a reminder to get out and vote on the Georgia to reelect Jon Ossoff and down to the other statewide and local candidates that are working hard to take this state in a new direction. It was truly an honor so be able to see Obama speak in Georgia and a memory that will remain ingrained within me and keep me motivated for this election, and all of the pressure we make in the future. And great thanks to all the other speakers such as Josh Mclaurin, Raphael Warnock, and some others, and the music that made it a great time. Obama please come to Georgia more, we need you!! 💙🍑

The one and only @barackobama @jonossoff @keishabottoms

#georgia
#obama
#vote
#electionday
#november3rd

Knowing your rights makes you a stronger voter. Here’s what to remember on November 3:

✊🏾 Polls in Connecticut open at 6 AM and close at 8 PM
✊🏾 If you’re in line when polls close, you can still vote
✊🏾 You can ask for assistance if you need help marking your ballot
✊🏾 If your eligibility is questioned, you have the right to cast a provisional ballot
✊🏾 Same-Day Registration (SDR) is available to all residents who are
eligible to vote

Not sure if you’re registered? Check your status and find your polling place at MYVOTE.CT.GOV before Election Day. 🗳️

Informed sisters lead strong communities. 💕

#AKA1908 #KnowYourRights #ThetaTauOmega #ElectionDay #VoteCT

🚨 BREAKING NEWS | OCTOBER 29, 2026 🚨

🇺🇸 🗳️ OVER 39 MILLION AMERICANS HAVE ALREADY VOTED!

With the 2026 midterm elections just 5 days away, early voting has surpassed 39 million ballots nationwide!

📊 Reports highlight significant participation among Black, Hispanic, and unaffiliated voters as Americans head to the polls ahead of Election Day.

⚖️ IMPORTANT: Early voting totals are NOT election results, and turnout alone does not determine which political party will win.

🇺🇸 Election Day: November 3, 2026.

Your vote. Your voice. Your future.

#MeganUnfiltered0 #BreakingNews #Midterms2026 #EarlyVoting #Election2026

item.caption:
When your job knows how to WORK HARD and PLAY HARD!!! 🙌🏽🔥

Our SARC Halloween Party was EVERYTHING!!! 🎉 From trivia and games to mummy wrapping, pizza, ice cream, and nonstop laughter… we had an absolute BALL!!! 🍕🍦😂

And guess what?! Ya girl, LITTLE BO PEEP, brought home 3RD PLACE in the costume contest!!! 🏆🐑💅🏽😂💕

But beyond the costumes, fun, and festivities, what means the most is being part of a team that continues to make me feel SEEN, VALUED, APPRECIATED, and SUPPORTED! ❤️ The SARC team truly knows how to make the workplace feel like FAMILY, and I don’t take that for granted! 🥹💖

And one more thing… Little Bo Peep didn’t just show up and show out…. SHE VOTED TOO!!! 🐑🗳️🇺🇸

I DID MY PART… DID YOU?! 🙏🏿🙏🏿🙏🏿

#LittleBoPeep #HalloweenFun #SARCFamily #IVoted #BlackDeafStudentsMatter

No matter what you believe in, every vote counts and it’s our chance to make our voices heard. Whether you’re voting early, requesting a mail-in ballot, or heading to the polls on November 3rd, make sure you have your plan ready.

Head to the link in my bio or visit vote.org to check your key dates, find your polling place, and get your voting plan set up today! 

#MakeAPlan #Vote #Maine #VoteOrg #electionday

Still have your mail ballot at home? Don't mail it: drop it off in person.
Official information: https://www.votemiamidade.gov/elections/voters/vote-by-mail.page

It must ARRIVE by 7 PM on Tuesday, November 3.

Through Sunday, November 1, 7 AM to 7 PM: at the staffed drop box at the Aventura Library (2930 Aventura Blvd) or any early voting site.
On Tuesday, Nov 3: only at the Elections offices, 2700 NW 87th Ave or 111 NW 1st St (lobby), before 7 PM. Precincts can't accept it.

Don't forget to sign the envelope.

I am option 101 on the ballot.

Dr. Prince Mapp

item.caption:
🎉 You Voted? You're Amazing! Now Pass it Along! 🗳️✨

Checking that off your to-do list feels incredible, but your civic superpower doesn't stop at the drop box—the real impact happens when you encourage others to vote too! 🤝

If you’ve already cast your ballot, take 5 minutes today to spark a chain reaction.📲 Text 3 friends or family members to ask if they have voted. If they haven't:

🚗 Offer a ride to a drop box. 
💬 Share your "I Voted" selfie to inspire your feed—peer-to-peer encouragement (and prodding) helps boost turnout. 
📋 Send helpful links (like ballot drop box locations) to first-time voters in your circle and tell them they’ve got this.

You’ve done your part—now help someone else raise their voice!📣💙

#IVoted #PassTheMic #VoteTogether #TurnoutTheVote #CivicEngagement #YourVoteMatters

item.authorHandle: iecsouthafrica
item.caption:
🗳️VOTING STATIONS ARE FOR VOTING, NOT CAMPAIGNING

On Election Day, political candidates, party leaders, and party agents are strictly prohibited from wearing political party regalia inside voting stations. 

Why? 
Because a voting station must provide a neutral environment where every voter can make their choice freely, without being influenced, pressured, or intimidated. 

What about voters? 
As a voter, you have the right to wear your party regalia to vote. However, no active campaigning, rallying, or distribution of party materials is allowed by anyone within the voting station boundaries.

When you arrive, the focus should remain entirely on your right to cast your ballot freely and in secret. 

#LGE2026 #GetUpShowUpVote #ElectionDay #YourVoteYourChoice

item.caption:
I swear, the strangest things happen to me. 🤣🤣🤣

Sitting in my getting-ready chair this morning, combing my hair… a simple task, you would THINK! 👀

Comb gets stuck.
“What the heck?”
Comb again.
“WHAT is in my hair?!”

So I grab that section and investigate… MY “I VOTED” STICKER! 🤦🏼‍♀️🤣🤣🤣

Apparently, it had moved from my shirt to my hair and was campaigning for a permanent position. 🙄😂

Getting it out cost me a few hairs. I voted, but my roots demanded a RECOUNT! 🤣🤣🤣

Anyways… GOOD MORNING! May your morning drink be strong and your stickers stay where you put them! ☕️🤪

#RogueSticker #IVoted #HairTodayGoneTomorrow #Morning Shenanigans #YouCantMakeThisStuffUp #GoodMorningYall

Your vote is your choice and your choice only. 

Make your vote count.

author: lauraphierro

item.authorHandle: lauraphierro
item.caption:
🇺🇸❤️ I voted because this country is part of my dream.

  Como inmigrante, sé lo que significa llegar a un país con sueños, esperanzas y ganas de salir adelante. También sé lo que cuesta construir algo desde cero, luchar por una oportunidad y convertir una idea en una pequeña empresa.
 Hoy voté porque creo en el poder de nuestra voz, en las oportunidades para quienes trabajamos por nuestros sueños y en un futuro donde los pequeños negocios puedan crecer, las familias puedan prosperar y las próximas generaciones tengan oportunidades para alcanzar sus metas.
 Detrás de cada pequeño negocio hay una historia, sacrificios, noches de incertidumbre y una enorme ilusión por salir adelante. El mío es uno de esos sueños. ❤️
 No importa de dónde venimos; todos queremos un país donde el esfuerzo tenga valor, donde podamos construir un futuro mejor y donde nuestros sueños tengan la oportunidad de convertirse en realidad. 🇺🇸
 As an immigrant, I know what it means to come to a country with dreams, hope, and the determination to build a better future. I also know how hard it is to build something from the ground up, fight for opportunities, and turn an idea into a small business.
 Today, I voted because I believe in the power of our voices, in opportunities for those who work hard to achieve their dreams, and in a future where small businesses can grow, families can thrive, and the next generation has the opportunity to reach its full potential.
 Behind every small business is a story of sacrifice, sleepless nights, moments of uncertainty, and an unwavering desire to succeed. Mine is one of those stories. ❤️
 No matter where we come from, we all want a country where hard work matters, where we can build a better future, and where our dreams have the opportunity to become reality.

My vote is my voice, my hope, and my commitment to the future I want to help build. 🇺🇸 @bundtandbasque 
 #IVoted #ImmigrantEntrepreneur #SmallBusinessOwner #AmericanDream #smallbusinessmatters

Some Centre County voters will head to new polling places Tuesday for the general election as the county moves to meet federal accessibility requirements. 

Eight precincts in the State College and Bellefonte areas were updated since the primary to ensure compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, a 1990 federal law that prohibits discrimination on the basis of disability.

Voters can look up their polling place by visiting pavoterservices.pa.gov/Pages/PollingPlaceInfo.aspx

Visit centredaily.com to read the full story. 

Story by Bret Pallotto / Centre Daily Times
Photo by Abby Drey / Centre Daily Times 

#elections #pollingplace

author: gabbyrichards

item.authorHandle: gabbyrichards
item.caption:
Registered AND voted on the same day. 🗳️✨
.
I moved to Baltimore this summer, and this week I walked into my early voting center, registered, and cast my ballot in one trip. No hoops. No stress.
.
This is what democracy is supposed to feel like.
.
Early voting and same-day registration should be the standard in every state. Not a perk. Not a privilege. The standard. Especially right now, when the right to vote is under attack through purged rolls, extra paperwork, and fewer polling places. Those aren’t safeguards. They’re barriers. 🚫
.
Millennials and Gen Z: we have the potential to be the largest, most powerful voting bloc in this country. We just have to show up.
.
I know everything feels like it’s on fire and exactly the same at the same time. I feel it too. But not voting doesn’t punish the people you think it does. It doesn’t motivate the people in power to listen to us — it encourages them to just keep going more of the same BS. And we’ll inherit their mess. 
.
We care. Let’s prove it. Go vote. 🔥￼

Find your early voting options and GO. 👇 Link in bio.

#IVoted #VotingRights #EarlyVoting #fyp #baltimore

author: ashley_hufford

item.authorHandle: ashley_hufford
item.caption:
DO YOU HAVE YOUR VOTING PLAN YET?! 🗳️💙

We are FIVE DAYS away from perhaps the most critical election of our lives. (And I am PRAYING for the day when every election doesn’t feel like the most critical election of our lives. PLEASE.)

I’ve spent the last month going from Ohio to North Carolina to Michigan and back again with our fearless leader Katie Paris, our girl Heather Cox Richardson, and truly the best team anyone could ever dream of.

We’re not quite done yet (one last event this weekend!), but WHAT. A. RIDE. 💙

So many incredible people, so many important conversations, so much hope, and of course a few side quests along the way

But here’s my reminder: Election Day is just the LAST day to vote, not the ONLY day to vote!!!

Make your voting plan. Talk to your friends. Talk to your family. Talk to your neighbors. Make sure you know when, where, and how you’re voting.

And if you have questions, PLEASE ask! I’m always happy to chat. 💙

#electionday #heathercoxrichardson #maybehappyending #votevotevote #earlyvoting

item.caption:
🗳️ Your vote is your voice. 💛❤️

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, and every ballot helps shape the communities we live in, lead in, and serve.

⏰ Florida Noles: early voting ends this weekend. Depending on your county, the last day is Saturday, October 31 or Sunday, November 1. 
📍Outside of Florida? Early voting dates vary by state, so check your local election office.

Before you head out:
✅ Confirm your voter registration status
✅ Find your polling or early voting location
✅ Review your sample ballot
✅ Bring the required ID

Find your state’s election info at vote.gov, or visit dos.fl.gov/elections in Florida. 🍢

Make a plan, bring someone with you, and be sure you get out here and VOTE🚨

Tag us in your pics and see you at the polls!

#FSUBlackAlumni #ElectionDay #YourVoteYourVoice #GoNoles #Vote2026

item.caption:
Election Day is next Tuesday, Nov. 3. If you're with a campaign or issue group planning one more weekend of door-to-door, give us a call about door hangers and handouts.

For everyone else, the weeks after the election are a good time to plan your next business postcard. Once political mail slows down, a postcard about your services, an open enrollment, or your holiday hours has an easier time getting noticed. Tutoring centers, salons, restaurants, and home services can mail to their customer list or use Every Door Direct Mail to reach the neighborhoods around them.

We print postcards for Omaha businesses, schools, and organizations, and we can help with the design and the mailing.

item.caption:
Earlier this week, five students had the opportunity to represent the School of the Arts at a Governor's Candidate Forum hosted by ISU. Gubernatorial candidates Terri Pickens and John Stegner joined representatives from many colleges at ISU to answer questions the students had prepared in regards to their areas of interest/study. Representing the School of the Arts was art student Amanda Coburn, music students Amiah Heath and Brenna Scheffelmaer, and theatre students James Baum and Hannah Jensen. We are proud of these students for representing our School in this exciting forum! Election Day is November 3rd! Get out there and vote!

#isuschoolofthearts #vote #electionday #idahostateuniversity

The battle for control of the Senate is coming down to a handful of states, and even traditionally Republican strongholds are now in play.

Fox News Power Rankings identify South Carolina, Texas, Iowa, Alaska, Michigan and Maine as toss-ups heading into Tuesday's midterm elections.

South Carolina is the latest addition to the competitive category, while polling in Iowa shows a margin of less than one percentage point.

Download the FOX News app to follow this developing story.

Nearly 40 million early and mail votes are already in, running ahead of the 2022 pace. But roughly 29 million mail ballots haven't been returned yet.

Mail is too slow now. If your ballot is still on the counter, take it to an official drop box or your county elections office today, or vote in person.

Check your registration, find your drop box or polling place, and see your state's hours at vote.gov. Then write down your day, your time, and how you'll get there.

item.authorHandle: khmermaine
item.caption:
KHMER MAINE VOTER GUIDE: Election Day in Maine is Tuesday, November 3. Swipe through for a quick, easy-to-read guide to voting this year 🗳️

✅ Polls open between 6 and 8 AM (depends on your town) and close at 8 PM. If you're in line by 8 PM, you can still vote.
✅ Not registered yet? You can register in person at your town hall or at your polling place on Election Day.
✅ Registered voters do not need ID to vote. Bring ID and proof of address if you're a first-time voter, have moved, or are registering that day.
✅ Ranked Choice Voting is used for U.S. Senate and U.S. House, but not for Governor.

You'll also find statements from the candidates for Governor and U.S. Senate, in their own words and unedited.

Questions? Call or text the Voter Hotline at 207-558-3333 or email Vote@lwvme.org. Find your personalized ballot info at Vote411.org.

Information from the League of Women Voters of Maine Education Fund's nonpartisan voter guide. Also available in Khmer, Vietnamese, and Tagalog.

#SEAMEVOTE #Vote411 #ElectionDay #MaineElections2026

author: theequalvote

item.authorHandle: theequalvote
item.caption:
Don't like the candidates on your ballot? They were almost certainly chosen in the primaries using choose-one voting, meaning the lesser-evil issue likely played a role in who made it to the general election.

Even if you like some of the candidates on your ballot, vote-splitting might cause your vote to not carry the same weight as other voters in the general election.

STAR Voting fixes this problem. 👉  https://starvoting.org

#midterms #electionday #starvoting #votingreform

With Election Day less than a week away, this edition of Notes from the Third reflects on the conversations, experiences, and lessons from the campaign.

I've also added a new 'Candidate Resources' section to my campaign website, bringing together the candidate questionnaires, voter guides, profiles, and media coverage I've participated in throughout this election. I encourage everyone to explore these resources, compare candidates' positions, and make an informed decision.

Nebraska voters can check their registration status, find their polling location, and access election information through the Secretary of State's official voter portal:

https://votercheck.necvr.ne.gov

Regardless of how you vote, take time to understand the issues, make a plan, and participate.

Your vote. Your voice. Your future.

author: gabriella.m.nunez

item.authorHandle: gabriella.m.nunez
item.caption:
My dad always asks me “what have you done for your country today?”

Georgia, I voted! 🍑🗳️

I hear it among my friends, talking about child care, what it takes to buy our first homes, the cost of living, cool programs we hear about and walkable areas in our city. So much of that is rooted in our vote. 

I don’t take the opportunity to cast a ballot for granted. I grew up understanding that having a voice in the democratic process is a privilege not everyone gets to experience. And there’s something special about showing up in person, standing in line with your neighbors and participating in a process that’s bigger than any one of us (in Georgia it feels high-tech too). 

Whatever your political beliefs, I hope you’ll take the time to get informed, ask questions and make your voice count.

You can vote early through Oct. 30. Election Day is Nov. 3. 

Peach State, see you at the polls! 🍑

#GeorgiaVotes #IVoted

Election Day is Nov. 3. Have you turned in your ballot yet?
Visit the link in bio for our guide to Oregon’s November election.
Reminder: voters have until Election Day on Nov. 3 to submit their ballots. Ballots must be postmarked by Election Day or dropped in official drop boxes by 8 p.m. State and local officials recommend voters use ballot drop boxes whenever possible.

🗳️There's Still Time to Vote Early!

Election Day is right around the corner, but you don't have to wait until November 3 to cast your ballot!

Charleston County residents can vote early through Saturday, October 31, until 6 PM at any of the following Early Voting locations:

- County Voter Registration and Elections Office – 4340 Corporate Rd., North Charleston
- James Island Baxter-Patrick Library – 1858 S. Grimball Rd., James Island
- Morris Brown AME Church – 13 Morris St., Charleston
- Greater Macedonia AME Church – 725 Savage Rd., Charleston
- Seacoast Church – 750 Long Point Rd., Mt. Pleasant
- St. John's Episcopal Church – 3673 Maybank Hwy., Johns Island
- St. Paul's Hollywood Library – 5130 Highway 165, Hollywood

🇺🇸 Voting on Election Day instead?

Polls will be open on Tuesday, November 3, until 7 PM. Voters must cast their ballots at their assigned polling place. Anyone in line by 7 PM will still be allowed to vote.

🔎 Find your assigned Election Day polling place at https://vrems.scvotes.sc.gov.

Make your voice heard, James Island!

item.authorHandle: khmermaine
item.caption:
TAGALOG MAINE VOTER GUIDE (full e-guide available at sea-maine.org): Election Day in Maine is Tuesday, November 3. Swipe through for a quick, easy-to-read guide to voting this year 🗳️

✅ Polls open between 6 and 8 AM (depends on your town) and close at 8 PM. If you're in line by 8 PM, you can still vote.
✅ Not registered yet? You can register in person at your town hall or at your polling place on Election Day.
✅ Registered voters do not need ID to vote. Bring ID and proof of address if you're a first-time voter, have moved, or are registering that day.
✅ Ranked Choice Voting is used for U.S. Senate and U.S. House, but not for Governor.

You'll also find statements from the candidates for Governor and U.S. Senate, in their own words and unedited.

Questions? Call or text the Voter Hotline at 207-558-3333 or email Vote@lwvme.org. Find your personalized ballot info at Vote411.org.

Information from the League of Women Voters of Maine Education Fund's nonpartisan voter guide. Also available in Khmer, Vietnamese, and Tagalog.

#SEAMEVOTE #Vote411 #ElectionDay #MaineElections2026

item.caption:
🇺🇸🗳️ I VOTED! ❤️🤍💙

Just finished casting my vote in the midterm elections, and I’m proud to have made my voice heard!

I truly believe that if we want to see change, we have to be willing to stand up and be part of it. We can’t just hope things will get better — we have to do our part to make a difference.

I know my one vote may seem small, but it matters to me. It represents my voice, my values, and the future I hope to see for our families and generations to come.

So here’s my little reminder to everyone: Get out and VOTE! 🇺🇸 Don’t ever think your voice doesn’t matter, because it absolutely does!

Change starts with us, and every single vote counts! ❤️🤍💙

#IVoted #MyVoiceMatters #EveryVoteCounts #BeTheChange#2026midtermelection

author: dominicanabroad

item.authorHandle: dominicanabroad
item.caption:
🇺🇸 47 out of 50 states ALLOW EARLY VOTING! With everything going on in the world right now, the midterm elections on November 3 are one of the most important in recent history.

I highly recommend EARLY VOTING, especially if you have commitments, don’t want to wait in long lines, etc.

For NYC: You can find your pollsites at findmypollsite.vote.nyc and the wait times on this map vote.nyc/page/wait-time-map.

To check your poll site go to VOTE.ORG (the one in the video) or USA.GOV.

Still need to register? vote.gov is the place to start.

Heads up: YOUR EARLY VOTING SITE MAY NOT BE YOUR ELECTION DAY SITE.

Go vote!! 💙💙💙💙💙

#vote #earlyvoting #midterms #nyc #ivoted

author: mylylive

item.authorHandle: mylylive
item.caption:
Actually, Pam, its been a rough couple of months 🫩 particularly with regards to our government and economy..

election day is a week from today! 
✉️ If you plan to vote absentee, remember to get those ballots in! 
🚶‍♀️If you plan to vote in person on election day, now is a great time to start thinking ahead for it!
*if you are unsure of your voting location, you can go to vote.org to find it & plan ahead! 

Our votes won’t lead to instant change, but they are still so important. This is how we take steps in the right direction! 

🧤for my fellow Michiganders:
I found a really great resource at voterguide.planetdetroit.org - the page lists all Michigan candidates, links to associated articles for each, as well as a breakdown of where each candidate has gotten their campaign funding. If you want to do any more research before you cast your vote, check this out!! 

Yay democracy!!! Go get that sticker!! ☺️🥳❤️‍🔥🤍💙🖤🎉 

#vote

Guess what day it is?!?!

It's Wednesday, and that means ONLY 2 MORE DAYS OF EARLY VOTING! 🗳️

Don't let Friday sneak up on you! Early voting ends October 30, and Election Day is November 3!

Get out there and make your voice heard!

📍 Find voting information at www.votetexas.gov

#HumpDay #EarlyVoting #LeagueCity #Election2026

author: napcast206

item.authorHandle: napcast206
item.caption:
Democracy doesn’t start and end at the ballot box. It starts with how we raise, teach, and show up for children.

It starts when we teach children that fairness matters. That their voices matter. That everyone deserves dignity. And when something isn’t fair, we don’t just accept it. We speak up and work together to make it better.

Because voting matters. A LOT. The people we elect shape the policies, funding, and conditions that affect our children, families, schools, and communities.

But we can’t wait until children are old enough to vote to teach them what it means to participate in a democracy. And we can’t cast our ballots, pat ourselves on the back, and call it a day.

On this episode of #Napcast, we explore what it means to show up for our communities. Because building the world we want takes more than a trip to the polls. It takes practice, participation, and all of us.

With the midterms approaching, here’s your reminder:

🎧 1. Listen to the episode! Avail wherever you listen including: https://open.spotify.com/episode/3rONgRdhSpfXEofjXg1t35

🗳️ 2. Learn what’s on your ballot. Understand the candidates and measures that affect your community.

📅 3. Make a plan to vote. Consider voting early so you have time to address any issues.

📣 4. Talk to your people. Share resources, help folxs find voting information, and mobilize your community. Keep showing up long after #ElectionDay.

🌱 5. Start with the children in your life. Model fairness. Make room for their voices. Help them recognize injustice and practice working together toward something better.

Voting is a powerful tool. But democracy is also what we practice in our homes, classrooms, neighborhoods, and communities every single day.

So, what are we teaching the next generation about having a voice and what to do with it?

I just voted! 🗳️

I cast my ballot, and it felt good to have my voice counted in decisions that shape our schools, our courts, and our community.

If you haven't voted yet, tomorrow (Friday, Oct. 30) is the last day of early voting. In Brazoria County, polls are open 7 AM – 7 PM, and you can vote at any early voting location. If you miss it, Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3.

Look up your sample ballot before you go so you're ready, and bring a friend.

Your vote is your voice. Use it, this is a serious matter! 💕💚💕💙💕

#IVoted #EarlyVoting #BrazoriaCounty #Pearland

Your vote is your voice. Use it, this is a serious matter! 💕💚💕💙💕

That stop comes after dueling rallies in another key state offered a snapshot of the divisions shaping the midterm elections.

Liz Landers reports.

item.caption:
If you're voting on election day, that means you're voting on election day. Even if you have to walk a mile in a storm and wait 3 hours in a line to do it.

item.caption:
Election exhaustion is real, but our future is worth showing up for! We’re tired of the endless headlines, political drama, attack ads, and nonstop noise. But we cannot afford to tune out when so much is at stake.

President Trump is crisscrossing the country, bringing the energy and making the case. Now it’s our turn to deliver. No sitting on the sidelines. No assuming someone else will do it. No taking our future for granted!

I know we’re frustrated. The war, high oil prices, grocery bills, and our mounting national debt are real concerns. We want answers, and we want results. President Trump has two more years in this term to push his agenda forward and pull us out of this mess. He has every incentive to fight for the policies he believes in, tackle the problems facing our country, and work to shape the legacy he leaves behind. He hates losing more than anything, and I know he will make changes with whomever or whatever it takes to bring this country back.

So don’t let election fatigue silence your voice. We didn’t come this far to sit this one out. The future is shaped by those who show up. Enough talk. Enough excuses. 

GET OUT & VOTE! GOD BLESS AMERICA! 🙏

#AmericaFirst #Midterms2026 #Trump #ElectionDay #MakeYourVoiceHeard #WeThePeople

DOJ monitors are coming to Mecklenburg. Know your rights.

DOJ election monitors are coming to Mecklenburg on Election Day, Nov. 3.

They can watch setup and talk to voters outside the buffer zone — but they can't be in the voting area while people vote, and you don't have to talk to them.

🗳️ Election Day: Tuesday, Nov. 3, polls open 6:30am–7:30pm
📞 Problems? Mecklenburg Board of Elections: 704-336-2133
